title: Some results on small ordered and cyclic Ramsey numbers
summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k$ be simple graphs such that for each $j \in \{ 1, 2, \ldots, k \}$, the vertex set of $H_j$ is $\{ 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n_j - 1 \}$ for some $n_j \in \mathbb{N}$. The ordered Ramsey number $R_\mathrm{ord}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is the smallest $n \in \mathbb{N}$ for which every $k$-edge-coloring of the complete graph on the vertex set $\{ 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1 \}$ contains $H_j$ as a monochromatic subgraph of color $j$ for some $j \in \{ 1, 2, \ldots, k \}$, with the vertices appearing in the same order as in $H_j$.
